text: It is medieval fantasy TPP hack-n-slash with bits of platforming actions. Looks decent and level design lets you have some fun looking for hidden treasures. But fighting is boring. Like really boring. It just doesnt work at all. And as for h-n-s it is major issue so nothing can save this game. On the bright side game has two nice 'twists' that could interest somebody. First is multiple of characters to play as. During missions you can meet some NPCs in trouble and if you manage to save them they will join you and act as playable characters for the rest of the game. On the other hand this undefined main character causes story to be unrelated to characters. So dont expect any story from this game. Just almost random stages, enemies and your character of choice. It could be arena-type game and it wouldnt be any different. Next 'twist' is that you can outfit your hero before every mission. Equipping your character is based on limited budget mechanic. Every piece of gold you collected adds to the pool of gold which limits gear you can wear. Every piece of equipment substracts from this pool so you have to pick if you prefer balanced setup with average elements or maybe you will sacrifice armor in favor of better weapon. You cant pick your playstyle and enjoy the game your way without being forced to play some fixed archetype. Mentioned gold you receive for completing every mission and even more you can find during the mission as extra hidden treasures that require from you taking extra risk. And risk here is high - death equals restart of the level. But thats fine, levels are short and fun part is mastering every level. To sum it up: game is quite interesting and as such curiosity you could grab it to have a look, but i was unable to finish it - simplistic fighting mechanics are boring and no amount of customisation of character can change that.

title: enclave
text: Enclave is a fantasy action game. You unlock new characters with different weapons and abilities as you play and depending on your saved budget and unlocked items, you can equip your selected character with a choice of weps, armor and potions, and thats pretty much all the "rpg" aspect. The game has a story which is not bad but pretty basic and you can play it from the perspective of two opposing factions, you can chose the "light" or dark" campaign at the begining of the game and you will get to play different characters with different stories. The game stands out by its very well made fantasy setting and an excellent soundtrack. Personally i found the graphics and the music to be outstanding back in the day. The graphics aged of course but they aged quite well, for the most part they look good even by today standards. They might be technically dated but artistically they are still great. The combat is solid and quite varied for a hack and slash game. The choice of character is vital because the game is pretty difficult and some characters will do a lot better than others in certain levels. Every level can be completed with any character but the difference in difficulty can be unforgiving. The levels are not very big but most of them are intricated enough to allow some exploration in search for hidden stuff. It was one of my fave PC action games back in 2003 but i still enjoy playing it today.

text: This is a great space sim game and I'd strongly suggest you try it out. It's free so there's nothing to lose. You start off with a choice of three ships, a cargo ship, a transport ship and a fighter. The most obvious choice may be the fighter, but you'll find that the cargo ship's storage will come in handy for taking jobs and trading. I chose the cargo ship and after some grinding, I was finally able to upgrade. I eventually had a fleet of cargo ships and fighter escorts that protected my convoy as it moved through dangerous trade routes. The trade system is easy to use once you get a hang of it and it can be extremely rewarding to find a trade route that you can stick too. (Hint: try the rim to the alien worlds) The customization system for the ships can be confusing and hard to understand as there's no tutorial, but there are some hints for it. I like it if there were more options for fleet organization but for a free game this is impressive enough.

text: Endless Sky is a fun game if you are into trading simulations with a mix of combat. It does come off a bit lacking in depth though, focusing more on having a lot of different ships with a heavy amount of customization options you can do to those said ships. On a single play through you can spend hours doing what you want, and even though it can be quite grindy, it can be quite enjoyable. Perhaps the biggest draw to this game is that it is a free game and it is open source. Even if you perhaps are on the fence to playing this game, the fact that you won't be paying anything just to try it is a good reason to try it out and see what it might be like. title: enter the gungeon
text: Missed potential leaves what should be an entertaining dungeon crawler, a dull slow slog. - Gameplay At its heart, it has a good concept going that has moments of entertainments. The bullet hell designs of projectiles and dodging them is a nice take on the dungeon crawling formula. However, the first two floors are a painfully slow Russian Roulette where bad items means you might as well just call the run quits. And theres lots and lots of bad, borderline useless items and weapons that feel less like upgrades to your basic, and more like an alternative that requires extremely scarce ammo. This basically leads you to conserving your ammo until bosses, who take entirely too long to plink to death regardless, and only offer a challenge due to the fact that you might just die of boredom midfight. It only gets worse at floor 3+, where anything and everything takes an abysmally long time to kill. Luckily, one of my biggest complaints in regards to the design of the game was fixed in the form of end-floor quicksaves, something that should have existed in the first place, but at least allows someone who gets as bored with the game as I do a way of coming back to it later. + Visuals It looks fantastic, every creature and crevice is designed with love. Great designs and animations all around. + Audio The music is catchy, the noises of enemies and weaponry is quite adorable. I tried to like it, I really did. Its great in essentially all ways but gameplay, and I don't think they can ever fix it (or intend to fix it) in a way thats going to make it fun for me. As it is right now, its a boring chore to play that relies to heavily on a decent start to not turn into a bullet sponge hell that I tend to hate every minute of. I can't recommend it.

text: A difficult yet rewarding experience.  As you learn the game, sure, you may get mad from deaths.  However, once you get used to the game everything becomes amazing. There is always something to do in this game. I don't care what system you get this game for, GET IT.
